release_notes: **Shutdown lost committed data**: the shutdown re-encrypt wrote `performance.db.enc` from the main DB file only, so committed writes still in the WAL were missing from the snapshot; if removing the plaintext then failed, the next boot trusted the stale `.enc` and discarded them. The snapshot now goes through SQLite's backup API (includes WAL frames), a failed plaintext removal deletes the just-written `.enc`, and the boot-side guard keeps a newer plaintext. **Shutdown re-encrypt failing on open files**: 11 of 48 logged prod shutdowns failed to re-encrypt (WinError 32) because child processes (PositionEngines, in-flight runs) still held `performance.db`. On exit the app now stops the scheduler and child processes before re-encrypting (on `serve()` return and on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGBREAK), not via `atexit`. **Truncated `.enc` on a hard kill**: snapshots are written to a temp file, fsynced and renamed into place. The boot-side "plaintext is newer than the snapshot" guard now sets the snapshot aside as `.enc.stale-<timestamp>` instead of deleting it. Installer: NSSM stop stages raised to 15s each (default 1.5s), and the bounded-stop wait raised from 15s to 50s, so a normal shutdown is no longer cut off mid-write. Test suite no longer creates stray plaintext DBs in the real data root (`tests/conftest.py` repoints `DATA_ROOT` to a temp dir). `tools/fix_ledger_charges_2026_09_19.py`: checkpoints the WAL after applying and verifies the rows from the main file alone. Prod needs a full rebuild + reinstall for the code changes to take effect.
